The *Ekakauddesa* is the opening summary or exposition of single items (*ekaka*) in the *Puggalapaññatti*, the fourth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It serves as a doctrinal matrix (*mātikā*) or list of designations pertaining to categories of individuals and phenomena considered singly.

While no discussions of the text appear in the provided secondary literature dossier, SuttaCentral registers cross-references and conceptual parallels to canonical suttas and Abhidharma treatises, including the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Bahudhātuka Sutta* (MN 115), the *Indriyavibhaṅga* (Vb 5), the *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* (Vb 18), as well as the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* (discourses on the eighteen elements and four dhyānas) [SuttaCentral].
